The short version

This summary is here to help you. The full text below is what applies.

  • Brazos is a marketplace. Customers and Workers deal with each other directly. Brazos does not do the work and is not a party to any job.
  • Workers are independent contractors. They are not employees of Brazos (section 3).
  • Brazos does not run background checks and does not verify anyone's identity, licenses or insurance (section 5). You decide who you work with.
  • A job's payment is held until the Customer approves the work, with set rules for cancelling and refunds (section 4). A held payment is not insurance.
  • What you can recover from Brazos is limited (sections 7 to 10).
  • Disputes with Brazos are resolved one person at a time, in New York, with no class actions and no jury trial (section 17).
01

What Brazos is

Brazos is a marketplace for short-term local work. It lets people who need work done ("Customers") post jobs, and lets people willing to do that work ("Workers") find those jobs and bid on them. A Customer can also send a job request directly to a Worker. Once a Customer hires a Worker, the two can message each other about the job. Many users are both at different times.

Brazos provides the software and, through its payment provider, takes and holds payment for jobs booked in the app. Brazos does not provide the services listed on it. Every job is an agreement between a Customer and a Worker directly. Brazos is not a party to that agreement. Brazos is not an employer, a staffing agency, a contractor or a home-services company, and it does not supervise, direct or perform any work.

02

Who may use Brazos

You must be at least 18 years old and legally able to enter into contracts where you live. You must provide accurate registration details, including a real name and a working phone number, and keep them accurate.

One account per person. You may not use Brazos if Brazos has removed you from it before. You are responsible for everything done through your account, and for keeping your sign-in details secure: your password, or the codes sent to your phone. Tell us straight away if you think someone else has used your account.

Brazos is operated from the United States and is intended for use in the United States.

Text messages. If you sign in with your phone number, you agree to receive a text message with a one-time code each time you sign in. Message and data rates may apply.

Electronic records. You agree that Brazos may give you notices and records electronically: in the app, by notification, or through the phone number or email address on your account. Accepting these Terms in the app has the same effect as signing them.

03

Workers are independent contractors, not employees

This section is important and you should read all of it.

Workers who find jobs through Brazos are independent contractors. They are not employees, agents, partners, or joint venturers of Brazos, and nothing in these Terms or in how the platform works creates an employment relationship with Brazos. No Worker has authority to act or speak for Brazos.

Specifically, Brazos does not:

  • set a Worker's hours, schedule, or availability;
  • supervise, direct, or control how a Worker performs a job;
  • set the price a Worker offers;
  • require a Worker to accept any particular job, or any minimum number of jobs;
  • prevent a Worker from working for competitors, other platforms, or directly for their own customers;
  • provide tools, equipment, vehicles, or materials;
  • pay wages, overtime, or benefits, or withhold taxes.

As a Worker, you are solely responsible for your own taxes (including self-employment tax), your own insurance, any licenses or permits your work requires, and compliance with any laws that apply to the work you do. You decide which jobs to bid on and on what terms. You confirm that you are legally allowed to work in the United States.

Some work can only be done legally by a licensed professional. Do not offer work that needs a license you do not hold, and do not ask a Worker to do it.

Where the law requires it, Brazos or Stripe may report payments to tax authorities and may ask you for tax information first.

As a Customer, you are responsible for understanding that you are engaging an independent contractor directly, not hiring an employee of Brazos, and for whatever obligations that engagement creates for you under applicable law.

04

Payments

Payments in Brazos are processed by Stripe, our payment provider. Card details are entered into Stripe's own payment form and never reach Brazos.

  • Accepting a bid books and pays for the job. When a Customer accepts a bid, the Customer's card is charged the agreed price plus a Protection fee, and any tax that applies. Each amount is shown before the Customer pays.
  • What the Protection fee is. It pays for the held payment and the issue review this section describes. It is not insurance, a warranty, or a guarantee of anyone's work, and it does not cover injury, damage or loss.
  • The payment is held in protection. Brazos holds the payment, through Stripe, until the Customer approves the finished work. The Worker is not paid before then. No interest is paid on a held payment.
  • Brazos collects for the Worker. Each Worker appoints Brazos as the Worker's limited agent for one purpose only: collecting the Customer's payment for a job. Once a Customer has paid Brazos the agreed price, the Customer has paid the Worker for that job, and the Worker looks to Brazos for that money under these Terms.
  • Approval releases it. When the Customer approves, the payment is released to the Worker. If the Customer neither approves nor reports an issue within 72 hours of being told the work is complete, the payment is released automatically. In any case it is released 7 days after the work was marked complete, unless an issue or a card dispute is open.
  • Issues. If a Customer reports an issue with a job, the payment stays held until Brazos resolves it. Brazos reviews what both sides have put in the app and decides where the held payment goes. That decision settles the held payment only. It is not a ruling on anyone's legal rights, and it does not stop a Customer and a Worker from pursuing each other directly.
  • Workers are paid through Stripe. A Worker receives the agreed price less Brazos's fee, which the app shows before the Worker bids, into the payout account the Worker sets up with Stripe. Stripe's own schedule decides when that money reaches the Worker's bank.
  • Fees are fixed at booking. Brazos may change its fees, but the fees for a job are fixed when the job is booked.
  • Cancelling. A Customer may cancel a booked job. Cancelling is free more than 24 hours before the arrival window starts, within 15 minutes of hiring, or when the job has no scheduled date. A later cancellation, or one after the work has started, carries a cancellation fee that goes to the Worker; the rest is refunded. The Protection fee is refunded in full whenever a job is cancelled. If the Worker cancels, the Customer is refunded in full. If the Worker reports that the Customer was not there, the payment stays held until Brazos decides it. The app shows these terms before you pay, and the fee, if any, before you confirm a cancellation.
  • Refunds go back to the card that paid, on the provider's timeline.
  • Card disputes. If a Customer disputes a charge with their card issuer, Brazos may keep the payment held and may share the job's records with Stripe and the issuer.
  • Money paid by mistake or later reversed. If money that reached a Worker is later reversed by a card dispute, is owed back to the Customer under these Terms, or was paid in error, the Worker agrees that Brazos may recover it, including by taking it from later payouts.
  • Holds. Brazos may delay a payout while it looks into suspected fraud or a breach of these Terms, while an issue or a card dispute is open, or where the law requires.
  • Tips are optional. After a job's payment has reached the Worker, a Customer may add a tip. It is charged through Stripe, with any fee shown before you pay, and goes to the Worker.
  • Saved cards are optional. A Customer may choose to save a card for faster hiring. The card is stored by Stripe, not by Brazos, and can be removed at any time in Payment methods. While a card is saved, you authorize Brazos to charge it, through Stripe, for the jobs you book.

Stripe's terms for Workers. Payment processing services for Workers on Brazos are provided by Stripe and are subject to the Stripe Connected Account Agreement, which includes the Stripe Terms of Service (together, the "Stripe Services Agreement"). By agreeing to these Terms or continuing to operate as a Worker on Brazos, you agree to be bound by the Stripe Services Agreement, as Stripe may change it from time to time. As a condition of Brazos enabling payment processing services through Stripe, you agree to give Brazos accurate and complete information about yourself, and you authorize Brazos to share it, and transaction information related to your use of Stripe's payment processing services, with Stripe.

Payments arranged outside Brazos are outside these Terms, and Brazos is not responsible for non-payment, underpayment, or any other dispute about them.

05

No screening, no guarantee

BRAZOS DOES NOT PERFORM BACKGROUND CHECKS, CRIMINAL RECORD CHECKS, IDENTITY VERIFICATION, REFERENCE CHECKS, LICENSE VERIFICATION, OR INSURANCE VERIFICATION ON ANY USER, unless a specific check is explicitly described in the app at the time you use it.

Ratings and reviews are supplied by users, and the completion, on-time and response figures on a profile are calculated by Brazos from activity in the app. Brazos does not independently verify them and does not guarantee they are accurate.

Brazos does not guarantee:

  • that any Worker is skilled, qualified, licensed, insured, honest, or safe;
  • that any Customer will be present, or has described the job accurately;
  • that any job will be completed, completed on time, or completed to any standard;
  • that any listing or user profile is genuine.

You are responsible for deciding who you work with. Take the same precautions you would with anyone you met outside the app.

06

Your responsibility for safety

You are responsible for your own safety. Brazos strongly encourages you to:

  • meet in a way you are comfortable with, and tell someone where you are going;
  • agree scope and price in the app before work starts;
  • carry your own insurance appropriate to the work you do or commission;
  • stop and leave any situation that feels unsafe.

If you are in immediate danger, contact your local emergency services. Brazos is not an emergency service and cannot intervene in one.

Reporting, suspension and termination

Brazos provides in-app tools to block and report other users, and to report what they post — job posts, profiles, reviews and messages. Reports are reviewed by Brazos administrators. When you block someone, their posts, profile and reviews no longer appear to you, and they cannot message you or bid on your jobs.

Brazos may, at its discretion and with or without notice, remove content and restrict, suspend, or permanently terminate any account for a violation of these Terms, for conduct that puts other users at risk, or where required by law. A terminated user may not create a replacement account. When an account is suspended, its unfinished jobs are cancelled and any payment for them is refunded in full to the Customer. The exception is a suspended Customer's job on which work has already started: its payment stays held until Brazos reviews it.

Brazos may report conduct it believes is unlawful to the authorities, and may keep and share the related records with them.

You may stop using Brazos and delete your account at any time — see the Privacy Policy for what happens to your data.

Suspending or terminating an account is a decision about access to the platform. It is not a legal finding about the user, and it does not make Brazos responsible for that user's conduct.

Sections 3 to 10, 13, 17 and 19, and anything you owe at the time, continue to apply after your account ends.
